headline: High risk of prompt-injection, data leakage, and cascading errors from shared filesystem/MCP-style handoff between Gemini CLI and LangGraph.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Gemini CLI ingests files and MCP tool outputs, and LangGraph can route application-defined node outputs into downstream nodes. Because the pair can share files via filesystem/git and no provenance tracking is documented, attacker-controlled content from one can be treated as instructions by the other. This is a plausible default pathway, not merely manual copy-paste.
conditions: IF Gemini CLI reads a file or MCP output produced by LangGraph without provenance checks
IF LangGraph forwards Gemini CLI output into a node that interprets text as instructions
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to every handoff file or node output
Restrict shared directories to non-executable text only
Require a human review step before any tool-using prompt
Disable MCP tools for untrusted content paths
requires-engineering: implement content-signing or schema validation between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents read and write filesystem content, and Gemini CLI explicitly handles repo files, user-provided directories, and a Gemini API key while LangGraph stores graph state in a checkpointer. Shared workspace or checkpointer data can therefore leak sensitive code or state into the other agent's outputs or upstream model calls in default setups.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or repository
IF LangGraph checkpointer state contains secrets or sensitive documents
IF Gemini CLI is allowed to read files that LangGraph later serializes into prompts
mitigations: Separate workspaces and checkpointer stores
Move secrets out of shared directories
Redact sensitive fields before checkpointing
Limit Gemini CLI file access to a narrow allowlist
requires-engineering: add per-field encryption or secret-scanning gates

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Gemini CLI can write the filesystem and modify git state, while LangGraph can also write filesystem state through application-defined files and persistent checkpoints. The pair therefore has overlapping write authority over shared mutable resources, and the rubric treats same-dir git/filesystem writes without locks as high risk. No locking or coordination primitive is documented.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same git checkout
IF LangGraph persists checkpoints into a directory Gemini CLI can modify
IF either agent writes concurrently without an external lock
mitigations: Use separate git worktrees or repos
Serialize writes with a file lock
Disable git mutation in one agent
Keep LangGraph checkpoints outside the repo
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Gemini CLI can emit tool-using text and file edits, and LangGraph is explicitly a graph of nodes where developer-wired edges can treat prior outputs as inputs. If LangGraph consumes Gemini CLI output without verification, errors or fabricated facts can cascade into downstream actions or persisted state. The interaction is documented only at the library level, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF LangGraph uses Gemini CLI output as an authoritative node input
IF a downstream LangGraph node performs actions based on unverified text
IF no validation step checks Gemini CLI citations or structured output
mitigations: Insert a validation node between agents
Require structured JSON with schema checks
Add a human approval gate before side effects
Log and diff all propagated facts
requires-engineering: implement confidence-aware routing

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch stated. The only concrete compliance surface is that Gemini CLI handles a Google API key and LangGraph handles model-provider keys, so a breach would arise only if the operator routes regulated data into those external services. The other agent is not separately cited because no mismatch is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data is sent through either agent to a third-party model provider
IF the operator stores PHI or EU PII in shared checkpoints or repo files
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of prompts and checkpoints
Use a DPA-approved provider configuration
Disable logging of prompt contents
Review retention settings before deployment
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
